direction: A toy machine-learned interatomic potential: predict the energy of small Lennard-Jones clusters (5 to 13 atoms, random perturbations of minima and random configurations) from (a) raw coordinates, (b) sorted pairwise distances, (c) simple symmetry-function descriptors with permutation-invariant sum pooling. Compare kernel ridge regression and a small MLP on energy error, data efficiency, and behaviour under rotation and atom permutation of the test set.

notes.note: fix round: KRR re-run with wide grid, claims rewritten, 6 pages, READY

decisions.decision: Method = sum-pooled symmetry-function KRR (pre-registered as 'ours'); study is a controlled comparison, not a new method. Truncated sampling E<=50 because unbounded perturbation energies made MAE meaningless (found in smoke test before main runs).

Audit fix: the 5x5 KRR grid clipped SymFn-sum KRR at its smallest gamma/lambda. New grid for ALL KRR systems: gamma 10^-7..10^2 (half decades), lambda 10^-13..10^2 (decades), validation MAE selection, pairs with a failed or LAPACK-ill-conditioned Cholesky solve skipped. Grid bounds were fixed from validation errors only (no test numbers). Old KRR rows are superseded, not deleted; MLP rows are kept because the MLP code path is unchanged. Added grid-sensitivity (narrow/mid/wide), linear-ridge diagnostic, mean predictor at every n, and an untruncated-energy sanity run.
